deepAccepted.title: US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Broad Agency Announcement
deepAccepted.summary: This is a technically relevant Army Soldier Center BAA for METSS, particularly in chemical/biological protection, CBRN decontamination and survivability, protective and EMI-related materials, functional fluids, testing, and applied R&D transition/scale-up. The Official Grants.gov record expressly permits commercial firms, which conditionally supports METSS organizational eligibility. However, the available SAM.gov review contains only a webpage shell and does not provide the actual solicitation, active topics, required proposal content, mandatory registrations, restrictions, or evaluation criteria. Accordingly, METSS has evidence-backed technical relevance but not enough evidence for a responsible pursue decision or a defined prime/subcontract role. The Grants.gov record lists a response date of February 27, 2030, but current topic acceptance and solicitation status remain unverified.

(Approved METSS public profile) The BAA includes EMI/EMP protection and energy-efficiency research under Expeditionary Maneuver Support.: The synopsis lists "Energy efficiency, EMI/EMP protection, battlefield mobility" within Expeditionary Maneuver Support. (Official Grants.gov record) METSS has relevant materials and functional-fluid capabilities for harsh-environment and protective-material research.: METSS publicly identifies chemical-protective, electrostatic-dissipative, EMI, intumescent, self-sealing, and impact-resistant materials, plus polymers, coatings, adhesives, specialty chemistry, thermal-control fluids, lubricants, corrosion inhibitors, and other functional fluids. (Approved METSS public profile)

analysis.summary: This is a strategically relevant but highly open-ended NSWC Crane long-range BAA. METSS has evidence-backed potential contributions in advanced materials, protective/barrier materials, specialty chemistry and functional fluids, harsh-environment formulation and validation, process development, pilot-scale scale-up, and testing. Its documented past performance also supports a plausible defense-materials and survivability narrative. However, the reviewed opportunity does not identify a current materials- or chemistry-specific requirement, funding line, or defined work package. METSS should not commit to proposal development until it identifies a differentiated concept tied to a named Crane technical capability and obtains technical-POC confirmation that the concept is current, nonduplicative, and fundable. METSS could potentially act as a prime for a bounded materials/fluids/testing effort, but the public record does not establish METSS's desired role or the complete eligibility and resource prerequisites; role should be determined after concept and sponsor engagement.
analysis.immediate_action: Develop a one- to five-page, nonproprietary concept outline centered on a specific METSS-led technical work package—for example, harsh-environment material, protective/barrier material, specialty fluid, signature-management material, power-system material, or validation method—then contact the relevant NSWC Crane technical POC to confirm fit, current funding interest, principal/adjunct technical capability, nonduplication, security posture, and preferred submission path before preparing the required white paper. In parallel, internally verify SAM status, UEI/DUNS handling, available personnel/capacity, OCI, export-control implications, and whether METSS intends to prime or seek an integration partner.

deepAccepted.title: Advanced Manufacturing
deepAccepted.summary: PD-19-088Y is technically relevant to METSS’s broad applied-research identity, particularly advanced materials, specialty chemistry, process development, pilot-scale scale-up, and testing/validation. METSS has credible public evidence for a meaningful technical work package such as materials/process development, manufacturability studies, formulation and processing optimization, and performance/compatibility validation. However, this is framed as an NSF fundamental-research program, and neither current opportunity activity nor METSS’s administrative eligibility and proposal readiness is proven. Investigate rather than pursue now; a prime-versus-partner decision should follow confirmation of current status, NSF eligibility mechanics, and availability of a compelling fundamental research concept.
deepAccepted.why: The opportunity seeks fundamental, multidisciplinary advanced-manufacturing research, including materials processing, materials engineering and processing, manufacturing systems, equipment, methodologies, and cross-scale manufacturing.: The reviewed program description identifies these areas as examples and encourages interdisciplinary proposals that transform manufacturing capabilities, methods, and practices. (NSF Program Desccription PD-19-088Y) METSS has an evidence-backed technical basis for manufacturing-focused materials and chemistry work.: METSS publicly identifies organic materials, polymers, composites, coatings, adhesives, specialty resins, functional fluids, formulation/product development, mechanical and chemical engineering, and product/process design from laboratory development through commercial production. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS can contribute validation and transition-oriented work packages relevant to manufacturing-process and materials-development projects.: The profile identifies chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, and materials-compatibility testing, together with pilot-scale operations and light manufacturing. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has publicly documented prior work relevant to materials development, manufacturing scale-up, and industrial supply resilience.: Public examples include Advanced Lightweight Composite Structures for Ground Vehicle Systems; Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials; Critical Supply Chain Production of Energetic Materials and Associated Precursors; and DPA Title III Critical Chemicals Production. (Approved METSS public profile)

analysis.summary: This is a continuously open BAA through 04 January 2028, but it is not a general materials or CBRN funding vehicle: a concept must materially advance the DEVCOM Analysis Center analytic mission or an active DAC topic. analysis.summary: This is a strategically strong technical match for METSS’s applied-research identity in CBRN protection/decontamination, advanced polymers and barrier materials, specialty chemistry, and validation under harsh conditions. The strongest historical topic alignments were Amendment 2 B4 (PFAS-free omniphobic protective materials) and B6 (cross-linked polymer detection films), supported by both official topic scope and METSS public materials, chemistry, testing, and CBRN evidence. However, B1–B6 closed on March 2, 2026, and the supplied record does not establish an extension. METSS therefore should not treat the expired topics as available. A general-thrust Phase I submission may remain possible under the continuing BAA through September 30, 2034, but only after DTRA technical pre-coordination and confirmation of a viable funding path. METSS has an evidence-backed potential prime role for a materials/protection/decontamination-focused fundamental-research concept, but prime eligibility remains conditional on administrative and proposal-specific requirements.
analysis.immediate_action: Within the next business day, contact the listed DTRA BAA mailbox to confirm whether a general-thrust white paper is currently being accepted, identify the appropriate technical point of contact, and ask whether any B4/B6 successor, reopened topic, or related active call exists. In parallel, internally verify METSS SAM/UEI/Grants.gov status and decide whether to develop a university-supported, broadly publishable general-thrust concept focused on PFAS-free chemical-protective materials, agent/decontaminant compatibility, or fundamental polymer-film protection/detection mechanisms.

analysis.summary: This continuously open ERDC BAA is strategically relevant to METSS's full applied-R&D profile, particularly for a narrowly framed materials, polymer/composite, functional-chemistry, environmental-treatment, contamination-mitigation, or validation concept. The opportunity is not yet a confirmed pursuit because the BAA requires one current topic-specific research concept and METSS's mandatory SAM status and topic-dependent compliance readiness are unknown. METSS has a credible potential work package, but neither a specific topic nor an evidence-backed prime/subcontract structure has been selected.
analysis.immediate_action: Conduct a topic-mapping and compliance gate within the current ERDC BAA: select one controlling April 2026 topic in GSL, EL, CERL, or CRREL that supports a defined METSS research hypothesis and measurable validation plan; verify the live laboratory portal accepts that topic and is open; verify active SAM status; then decide whether METSS can lead the five-page pre-proposal or needs a partner for field access, specialized research, or topic-specific restrictions. Submit only if the resulting concept is research-focused and all mandatory eligibility conditions can be evidenced.
caveats: The Grants.gov record lists a January 1, 2027 response date, while the April 2026 BAA states that it remains effective until superseded. The supplied laboratory intake pages show no actual closing date; live portal availability must be verified before submission.
The standalone Pre-Proposal Guidelines document was not supplied; detailed submission conclusions rely on the reviewed BAA and laboratory intake-page findings.
Topic-level funding, award counts, anticipated period of performance, and probability of award are not disclosed in the reviewed materials.

deepAccepted.type: Cooperative Agreement / Grant / Other / Procurement Contract
deepAccepted.summary: This is a strategically relevant broad DARPA BAA with plausible METSS work-package fit in advanced materials, specialty chemistry/functional fluids, test and validation, and manufacturing scale-up. METSS's public profile supports an initial investigation because TTO explicitly values manufacturability, production responsiveness, supply-chain alternatives, and accelerated testing. However, the BAA is not a generic materials or domestic-manufacturing solicitation: it requires a revolutionary, quantitatively defensible concept tied to DARPA military mission impact. No such METSS-specific concept, team, readiness confirmation, or DARPA engagement is supplied. Accordingly, technical relevance is meaningful but not yet sufficient for a pursue recommendation or a defined prime/subcontract role. The operative supplied schedule is an Executive Summary due April 17, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET and a full proposal due June 22, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET; a full proposal additionally requires DARPA's signed Encourage Full Proposal letter.

(Attachment_B_Proposal_Instructions_and_Volume_I_Template.docx) METSS has public testing and validation capabilities that could support an evidence-backed materials or manufacturing work package, including chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, materials-compatibility, field, and analytical testing.: The profile lists chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, materials-compatibility, chemical/biological field, and advanced analytical testing capabilities. analysis.summary: This is a strategically relevant broad DARPA BAA with plausible METSS work-package fit in advanced materials, specialty chemistry/functional fluids, test and validation, and manufacturing scale-up. METSS's public profile supports an initial investigation because TTO explicitly values manufacturability, production responsiveness, supply-chain alternatives, and accelerated testing. However, the BAA is not a generic materials or domestic-manufacturing solicitation: it requires a revolutionary, quantitatively defensible concept tied to DARPA military mission impact. No such METSS-specific concept, team, readiness confirmation, or DARPA engagement is supplied. Accordingly, technical relevance is meaningful but not yet sufficient for a pursue recommendation or a defined prime/subcontract role. The operative supplied schedule is an Executive Summary due April 17, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET and a full proposal due June 22, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET; a full proposal additionally requires DARPA's signed Encourage Full Proposal letter.
analysis.immediate_action: Before April 17, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET, conduct a rapid internal concept gate: identify one METSS-owned, non-generic revolutionary concept with a measurable TTO outcome in Design/Build/Buy or Surge and Sustain; confirm whether METSS already has an Executive Summary under DARPA review; verify SAM/responsibility, OCI, resource, pricing, and classification posture; and determine whether METSS will lead or needs a systems/transition partner. If these checks support a credible concept, submit a compliant two-page Executive Summary through DARPA BAAT—not Grants.gov—and use DARPA feedback to determine whether to prepare a full proposal. Do not commit to classified tasks or an OT cost-share position without separate verification.
caveats: The supplied SAM.gov material was not independently readable as a current opportunity-status record; timing is based on the supplied BAA and amendment findings.

analysis.summary: PAR-27-098 is potentially relevant only as a commercialization mechanism for a specific eligible NIH-funded technology, not as a broad applied-research or manufacturing solicitation. METSS's public profile supports a plausible technical subcontract or internal work package in materials/chemistry development, validation, compatibility testing, and scale-up. However, the public record does not establish the mandatory prior NIH SBIR/STTR Phase II/IIB award or other SBC and registration conditions. METSS should not commit to a prime pursuit unless those eligibility and project-linkage conditions are verified. A partner role may be viable if an eligible NIH Phase II/IIB awardee requires METSS's documented technical capabilities, but no partner or specific eligible project is currently evidenced.
analysis.immediate_action: Before the August 5, 2026 first submission cycle, conduct a short eligibility gate: verify whether METSS itself has a qualifying NIH SBIR/STTR Phase II/IIB award within 36 months; verify current SBC, ownership/control, affiliate-count, registration, PD/PI, and foreign-relationship status; and identify a specific commercializable technology aligned to a participating NIH component. If METSS lacks the qualifying NIH award, do not prime; instead, monitor for or selectively approach eligible NIH Phase II/IIB awardees needing materials, testing, formulation, or scale-up support.

deepAccepted.title: Limited Competition: Superfund Hazardous Substance Research and Training Program (P42 Clinical Trial Optional)
deepAccepted.summary: This is technically relevant as a university-led research-partner opportunity, not as a METSS prime opportunity. METSS has credible public capabilities for an environmental science and engineering subcontract focused on hazardous-substance reduction or treatment chemistry, decontamination-oriented methods, material/chemical compatibility, analytical characterization, and treatment-performance validation. However, the NOFO requires a large, integrated Superfund Research Program Center with mandatory biomedical and environmental science/engineering projects, required cores, translational engagement, and a domestic accredited higher-education applicant. METSS's public profile does not establish prime eligibility or the broader Center infrastructure. Pursue only if METSS can secure a credible university-led Center team and a defined, mandate-responsive technical package; otherwise do not invest in a standalone application effort.
deepAccepted.why: The opportunity requires an integrated environmental science and engineering research portfolio and requires at least one project addressing biological, chemical, or physical methods that reduce the amount and toxicity of hazardous substances.: The reviewed announcement requires 3–4 research projects integrating biomedical research and environmental science/engineering and states that at least one environmental science and engineering project must address SRP Mandate 4: methods to reduce hazardous-substance amount and toxicity. analysis.summary: This is strategically adjacent but not presently a standalone METSS opportunity based on approved public facts. METSS can plausibly contribute an evidence-backed materials, formulation, scale-up, stability, compatibility, or product-validation work package to a qualified burn-product team. The record does not establish that METSS itself possesses the required burn-focused product, proof of concept, prototype, TRL/KRL 4 maturity, burn-relevant PI, or regulatory/clinical translation foundation needed for a credible prime submission. Technical relevance therefore does not establish program eligibility or prime readiness.
analysis.immediate_action: Before the July 7, 2026, 5:00 p.m. Eastern preapplication deadline, conduct a rapid internal go/no-go verification: identify any METSS-owned burn-product asset meeting the documented TRL/KRL 4 and proof-of-concept threshold; confirm an eligible PI and active SAM/UEI/eBRAP/Grants.gov status; and, if no such asset exists, approach only qualified burn-product prime candidates with a narrowly defined METSS materials/formulation, scale-up, stability, compatibility, or validation subcontract work package. Do not initiate a METSS prime preapplication without written internal evidence closing the mandatory product-maturity and PI gaps.

METSS eligibility therefore cannot be confirmed from the approved evidence.

partner_needs: If METSS were to reconsider after resolving CESU eligibility, it would need an eligible CESU lead with documented wildlife molecular-parasitology and wildlife-diagnostic experience.

A qualified molecular parasitology PI and diagnostic laboratory team with demonstrated parasite assay development, validation, reference sequencing, GenBank deposition, and NWHC-training capability would be required.

Any partner arrangement would need to establish responsibility for required key-person disclosures, data-management planning, reporting, Federal data-access rights, and potential wildlife-specimen regulatory requirements.
analysis.summary: This is a specialized wildlife molecular-parasitology capacity-building cooperative agreement for USGS NWHC, not a general biological-testing opportunity. METSS has publicly documented BSL-2 and broad analytical/testing capabilities, creating limited adjacent technical relevance, but the approved profile does not establish the central wildlife parasitology, molecular-diagnostic, reference-sequencing, or training expertise. More importantly, CESU-partner eligibility is unproven and appears to be a mandatory recipient requirement. METSS therefore lacks an evidence-backed prime or partner work package and should not pursue on the current record.
analysis.immediate_action: Do not allocate proposal resources. If there is a strategic reason to preserve optionality, first verify through the live Grants.gov record and the USGS contact which CESU eligibility condition governs, whether METSS Corporation is an eligible participating partner, and whether the displayed Grants.gov response date of September 4, 2026 remains operative; proceed only if those threshold facts and a qualified wildlife molecular-parasitology partner/team can be documented.
caveats: The Official Grants.gov record displays a response date of September 4, 2026, while the complete document-review findings state that the supplied solicitation text did not contain a closing date. The live opportunity record should control for timing verification.

analysis.summary: This is a weak direct fit for METSS Corporation despite a limited overlap in laboratory testing and BSL-2/analytical capabilities. The official opportunity principally seeks sustainable global fungal-disease detection, diagnostic, surveillance, response, workforce, partnership, data, and public-health-system capacity. METSS's approved profile supports possible narrow laboratory-support or technical-assistance participation, but does not establish fungal-disease expertise, global public-health delivery, country relationships, or prime-recipient administrative capacity. METSS should not pursue as a standalone prime on the present record. Investigation is warranted only if an experienced eligible global-health prime identifies a material, allowable nonresearch work package for METSS and METSS can verify registration and resource prerequisites before the deadline.
analysis.immediate_action: Before committing bid resources, verify METSS's current SAM.gov/UEI and Grants.gov status and applicant classification; then contact the CDC program office or attend/review the informational-session materials to confirm whether the contemplated laboratory-support role is allowable. If no prime-led, evidence-backed, nonresearch METSS work package and required partner letters can be secured promptly, do not pursue.

analysis.summary: ECLIPSE is strategically adjacent to METSS's applied materials, chemistry, characterization, testing, and scale-up profile, especially for a plasma-surface-interaction, plasma-enabled coating/materials, plasma chemical-measurement, or plasma-enabled environmental-remediation concept. However, this is not a strong METSS standalone pursuit: the official program requires a fundamental plasma-science/engineering challenge, while METSS's approved public profile provides no plasma-specific technical capability or past-performance evidence. METSS has a plausible, meaningful research-partner role supporting materials formulation and response, analytical characterization, compatibility/performance testing, and transition-oriented validation under a plasma-science-led team. The relevant deadline is controlled by the receiving NSF program. Supplied ECLIPSE materials list windows through September 29, 2026 for several participating programs, September 1–30, 2026 for CHE CSDM-B, October/November 2026 windows for certain programs, and November 16, 2026 for PHY Plasma Physics; the receiving-program page must control because one CHE date is internally inconsistent.
